card.band: 8h. Quaternion conventions, inertia normalisation and the sparse mass-matrix layout are all easy to get slightly wrong. Frontier agents get serial chains but not ball/free joints or default inheritance. A weaker model stops at kinematics.
card.cheat: Importing the mujoco pip package. It is not installed in the image and the tests run offline. Hidden models are random, so outputs cannot be tabulated.
card.grading: Differential tests against a reference build, which is not in the image, on generated MJCF models (chains, trees, mixed joint types, a few hundred models and thousands of states). Compare xpos, xquat, qM, qfrc_bias and qacc with a relative tolerance of 1e-8. Score is the fraction passed per bucket.
card.reference: A reduced port of the upstream C code that we write, about 3-4k lines, matching the reference to tolerance. It passes every case.
card.task: /app ships a Python package skeleton and MJCF sample models. The agent ports the MJCF parser and compiler (bodies, joints, geoms, inertia computation, defaults) and the dynamics core (kinematics, CRB, RNE, mass matrix, forward/inverse dynamics, Euler integration) in NumPy, with an API mirroring MjModel/MjData.

blockers: The reference port (3-4k lines) is not written, so build cost is high (about 3-5 days)
Pip mujoco 3.16.0 renamed or changed API: MjData.qM is now MjData.M, and mj_fullM takes (m, d, dst). The oracle dump script must use these.
Only 3 models, 20 states each, were tested. Ball and free joint conventions are pinned by the outputs, but the 1e-8 tolerance against an independent port was not tested.
spike.commands_log: python3 -m venv; pip install numpy mujoco==3.16.0; run.py: 3 MJCF models (hinge/slide chain with euler frame; ball joints with armature; free joint with nested default classes, mesh, fullinertia) x 20 random states; mj_forward, mj_fullM, np.linalg.solve vs d.qacc; run twice and compared md5 of dumped xpos/xquat/M/qfrc_bias/qacc.
spike.headroom_note: Oracle is pip mujoco 3.16.0 wheel (installs fine online, our side only). Our NumPy port is not written; the spike only checked oracle determinism and that tolerance is attainable. Untouched skeleton has no implementation.
spike.notes: Both runs gave an identical md5 (800bac28cecfd56b95148ed26665b6d0), so the oracle is deterministic. An independent NumPy solve of qacc from the dumped dense M and qfrc_bias matched MuJoCo's qacc to a worst relative error of 2.4e-15 (chain), 1.2e-14 (ball) and 2.8e-13 (free). Maximum cond(M) was 358. That is far inside 1e-8, so the tolerance is reachable by valid alternative solvers. The 60 cases are the 3 models x 20 states. Not run: a reference port, the upstream C++ build (the probe's cmake fetch of eigen timed out, so the tree was never built) and the repo test suite. MuJoCo is open source and public, so the Band score is at risk of K8 or K9: an agent knows the outline, but a faithful port of the compiler (defaults, inertia from geoms, fullinertia) is large. The note about step 6 (C++ build) was skipped because the pip wheel is sufficient as the oracle. The step-4 suite check was not run.

full_card.band: 8h tier. Frontier agents likely finish serial chains and some trees; ball/free joints, default inheritance and inertia normalisation are the hard buckets. Weaker model stops at kinematics (xpos/xquat). No dated public evidence, so E0.
full_card.build_cost: 3-5 days: reference port 3-4k lines plus generator, oracle capture from pip mujoco, and 1e-8 matching debugging; smoke probe amber (no offline build recorded), so the upstream C++ build for oracle checks must be done fresh (est. 10-20 min on 8 cores, unverified).
full_card.deliverable: NumPy Python package: MJCF parser and compiler (bodies, joints hinge/slide/ball/free, geoms, inertia, defaults inheritance) plus dynamics core (kinematics, CRB, RNE, mass matrix, forward/inverse dynamics, Euler integration) with MjModel/MjData-style API.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Image must not contain mujoco or mujoco-mjx (verify no import succeeds in the grader image; block sys.modules hits); tests run offline; hidden models and expected outputs stay sealed; agent cannot ship a shim that reads reference outputs.
full_card.grading_surface: Sealed differential tests on a few hundred generated MJCF models (chains, trees, mixed joints) and thousands of states; compares xpos, xquat, qM, qfrc_bias, qacc at rel tol 1e-8; score = fraction passed per bucket.
full_card.local_fit: CPU-only Python and NumPy, stdlib XML; fits 8 cores / 16 GB; no GPU, no network at run time.
full_card.lookup: partial: mujoco-mjx (JAX) and the mujoco wheel are public and close in algorithm, but not installable offline and not a NumPy MJCF compiler; no public NumPy port found.
full_card.provenance: google-deepmind/mujoco @ 3.16.0 (Oct 14 2026), Apache-2.0, C++ with Python bindings; not a fork; repo not archived; 15.8k stars.
full_card.reference: Our reduced port of upstream C (about 3-4k lines) matching the reference build to tolerance; upstream oracle obtainable via PyPI mujoco wheel on our side only.
full_card.ships: /app: Python package skeleton plus sample MJCF models; no upstream C++ source, no mujoco wheel, no reference outputs.
full_card.similarity: Max L0 neighbour 0.185 (S-im-027), then 0.18 (S-im-028), 0.174 (S-im-014), tune-mjcf archive 0.166 (different deliverable: tuning). Below K1 threshold; sibling seeds S-im-027/028 should be checked for scope overlap before release.

Band.why: Frontier likely partial on chains and trees; full 0.9-of-reference pass uncertain; no dated public evidence, so capped at 3.

Build.why: Estimated 3-5 days including oracle capture and 1e-8 matching debugging; smoke probe amber.

Fit.why: CPU-only Python and NumPy; no kernel or network needs at run time.

Hor.why: Parser, compiler and dynamics core are sustained work over an 8h tier.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 allows shipping a reduced port with notice.

Multi.why: Buckets per joint type, per output quantity and per model family give steady partial credit.

Nov.why: Max neighbour 0.185 is above 0.15 but is a sibling seed; tune-mjcf is a different deliverable; not crowded.

Real.why: Real upstream Apache-2.0 release 3.16.0, Oct 14 2026, 15.8k stars, active repo.

Ref.why: Reference is our reduced port of upstream, not a full upstream reimplementation; matches to tolerance by design, but scope is reduced.

Seal.why: Upstream C++ is public on GitHub and well known in outline, but not in the image; oracle and hidden cases can be kept out.

Surf.why: Hundreds of generated models and thousands of states across five quantities; bucketed, not an unlimited executable oracle.

spike_plan.kill_if: Independent solve misses 1e-8 on more than 5% of states (tolerance unreachable for valid alternatives), or ball/free quaternion or inertia conventions cannot be pinned from the docs and outputs.
spike_plan.pass_if: Outputs are bit-identical across two runs; independent NumPy solve matches MuJoCo qacc within 1e-8 relative on at least 95% of states; ball and free joint conventions are pinned by at least one model.
steps: In a throwaway container with network (not the image), create a venv and pip install mujoco==3.16.0; confirm import works and record the version.
Write 3 MJCF models: a serial hinge chain, a tree with a ball joint, and a free-joint body with fullinertia geoms and a nested default class.
Run mj_forward and mj_inverse on 20 random states per model; dump xpos, xquat, qM (mj_fullM), qfrc_bias and qacc to files; run twice and diff for determinism.
Independently solve qacc = inv(qM) @ (qfrc_applied - qfrc_bias) in NumPy from the dumped qM and qfrc_bias; measure max relative error against MuJoCo qacc and the condition number of qM per model.
Check whether 1e-8 relative is reachable by an alternative valid solver order: if the independent solve misses 1e-8 on more than 5% of states, tolerance is too tight for valid implementations.
Only if the reference C++ build is needed: clone upstream at 3.16.0 in the container and time a cmake build with 8 cores, recording the wall time.

v1.summary: S-im-030 passes the real-source, licence and sealing gates: MuJoCo 3.16.0 is a real Apache-2.0 release, the oracle and reference stay out of the image, and the only public Python relative (mujoco-mjx) is JAX and not installable offline. The main risks are the 1e-8 tolerance against an alternative solver and whether a frontier agent can reach 0.9 of the reference in 8h on ball/free joints, so run the spike before committing.

v2.note: Strongest seed. The pip mujoco wheel is an executable oracle on our side, and a model generator gives an unlimited sealed surface with natural buckets (parser/defaults, inertia, kinematics, CRB/qM, RNE, forward/inverse). The reference port is still unwritten and the C++ build probe failed (fetch timeout), but the oracle does not need it. Risks the spike must pin: 1e-8 rel tolerance under different summation orders (use an abs+rel floor), principal-axis eigen sign/order conventions for fullinertia, and keeping contacts/constraints/meshes out of scope (disable constraints so qacc = M^-1(tau - bias + passive)). Check scope overlap with S-im-027/028.
